text: Chapter one introduced the idea that suppliers and customers sit on a shared party layer. This lesson opens that up for suppliers: which table stores their procurement attributes, how they connect back to identity, and where their sites and bank details live.

Supplier-level attributes live in POZ_SUPPLIERS, with primary key VENDOR_ID — a naming holdover from Oracle's older E-Business Suite terms, even though the Fusion screens always say "supplier." The supplier number itself sits in a SEGMENT1 column, the same flexfield pattern from the last lesson showing up again.

POZ_SUPPLIERS doesn't store the supplier's name directly. It carries a PARTY_ID column pointing back to HZ_PARTIES, the shared identity table. The supplier's actual name lives once in HZ_PARTIES; POZ_SUPPLIERS adds the procurement role on top. Need a supplier's name in a query? You're joining through PARTY_ID.

A supplier can transact from multiple addresses, and that detail lives in POZ_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL_M, keyed by VENDOR_SITE_ID with a VENDOR_ID foreign key back to the parent supplier. Each site carries its own flags — whether it's a valid pay site, a valid purchasing site, or both — detail that only ever lives at the site level.

One more piece: when a payment actually needs to go out, bank account details live in Oracle Payments schema tables prefixed I-B-Y, not on POZ_SUPPLIERS itself. Knowing that saves you a confused search later. Up next, lesson six: customers, and the fuller trading community architecture behind both sides of the business.
